answer: Costly continuation spiral**: each new identity must inherit and extend a prior identity's interaction history, verified by chained hashes. A clone starts a fresh spiral, so it lacks the accumulated history weight needed to transact above a low ceiling. Honest agents grow their spiral cheaply through use; attackers must pay to simulate months of genuine interactions per clone. A walnut-sized seed history is cheap, but forging depth scales linearly with clone count. Identities below threshold are flagged with a jade mark, blocking payouts.
